core_obligations: Identify the morphism of topoi (proof lines 4975-4984): the author produces the morphism i_f : Sh(T_tau) -> Sh((Sch/S)_tau) and computes the sections of pi_S^{-1}F over T as the sections of f_{small}^{-1}F over T_tau, which is the displayed formula.

Set up the fpqc gluing (proof lines 4987-4992): for an fpqc covering {g_i : T_i -> T}, the sheaf condition is spelled out as the statement that a section of F over T compatible with the pullbacks descends, and the author sets up the compatibility data.

Reduce to a covering argument (proof lines 4995-5005): for an object V -> T and a section t, one takes for each i the largest open W_i of T_i x_T V on which the pullback of t agrees with the descended section.

Finish by refining (proof lines 5008-5027): using the construction of the small inverse image, the author chooses a tau-covering of each T_i over which the agreement is achieved, and concludes that the pullbacks glue, which gives the fpqc sheaf condition.
proof_roadmap: Compute sections of pi_S^{-1}F through the small inverse image along the structure morphism of the object.
For an fpqc covering, spell out the sheaf condition as descent of compatible sections.
Take the maximal open pieces on which two sections agree and refine the covering until they cover.
difficulty_reason: The lemma describes the inverse image of a sheaf along the projection pi_S from the big Zariski or etale site of S to the small site: its sections over T -> S are the sections of f_{small}^{-1}F over T_tau, and it satisfies the sheaf condition for fpqc coverings (statement lines 4959-4973). The first part is a computation through the morphism of topoi induced by an object of the big site (proof lines 4975-4984). The second part is a genuine gluing argument: for an fpqc covering the author takes the largest open subsets on which two candidate sections agree, refines by tau-coverings of the members to make those opens cover, and concludes (proof lines 4987-5027). The non-formal content is that refinement argument. The claim is H2: one computation plus one explicit descent argument.
